tips.title: Production notes
items: For a portrait, describe the expression, gaze and light before listing skin, hair and fabric details.
For an infographic, set the reading order and exact labels. Check the lettering and any factual content in the result.
For an edit, give each reference a role and state what to preserve before what to change.
Before animation, check the face and hands, keep the silhouette readable and leave space for the camera move.

prompts.title: A neighbourhood story — STAY CURIOUS
prompts.prompt: A beautifully photographed live-action feature-film still, 16:9 widescreen. A fictional woman around twenty-eight with short dark curls and a textured deep-blue blazer steps out of a tiny neighborhood bakery, holding the door naturally for a fictional man around thirty-two in a charcoal jacket. They are caught in an unposed shared laugh as they begin to walk down the street, both faces clearly readable and full of character. Her hair and jacket move in a light breeze. Warm light from the bakery's open doorway and ovens spills onto their faces, contrasted with the cool blue-hour city outside. Three small adult pedestrians add life farther down the sidewalk. Behind the two main characters, an elegant physically painted street advertising panel reads exactly "STAY CURIOUS" in two large cream lines on a rich burgundy background. The letters are part of the real location and remain crisp and readable. Fine skin texture, individual hair strands, tactile wool and linen, delicate bakery steam and believable natural hands. Composition at waist-level with a 35mm cinema lens, foreground depth, subtly glowing practical lights, restrained grain and rich cinematic color separation. The people are the clear focus; the frame feels like the beginning of a human story and has breathing room for a future tracking shot. A premium film scene, not a posed fashion shoot or a product still life. One coherent photographic image, no collage, border or graphic title overlay.

faqs.q: How is Seedream 5.0 Pro different from Lite, Flash and 5.5?
faqs.a: Pro is a single-image 2K route for detailed portraits, campaign layouts and infographics. Lite supports image sets; Flash is the fast 5.0 variant; 5.5 adds a native transparent PNG option alongside its image generation and editing workflow.

faqs.q: Can I use several reference images?
faqs.a: Yes. Use up to 10 references to guide one generated image. Assign each image a role, such as the person, wardrobe, location or visual style.

faqs.q: Can Pro create text and infographics?
faqs.a: You can request exact wording, multilingual labels and a clear layout. Review every letter and verify the information in the finished image before publishing.
MaxVideoAI returns one 2K image per request with JPEG or PNG output. Choose Seedream 5.0 Lite for related image sets.

faqs.q: How do I prepare a still for animation?
faqs.a: Choose a readable pose, clear face and hands, and space around the subject. Save the selected still and plan the motion in a separate video model. The video generation has its own settings and quote.

referenceWorkflows.title: Direct the portrait
referenceWorkflows.body: Choose an expression, gaze and camera distance. Describe the light and a few physical details, such as hair strands, knitwear or the texture of skin.

referenceWorkflows.title: Structure the campaign
referenceWorkflows.body: Give the person, product and text clear positions in the frame. Put exact wording in quotation marks and define a simple reading order.

referenceWorkflows.title: Make a focused edit

referenceWorkflows.title: Prepare the opening frame

section.title: How to prompt Seedream Pro
section.intro: Write a visual brief with a clear subject and purpose. For people, start with the expression and action; for layouts, start with the reading order. Add camera, light, materials and exact text afterwards.
section.tip: For reference edits, write “preserve” and “change” instructions separately. Inspect faces, hands and text before approving the next image.

globalPrinciples: Give each person a clear expression, gaze and place in the frame.
Describe physical light and materials instead of adding a long list of quality adjectives.
For text, specify the exact words, hierarchy and position, then check the generated lettering.
Leave space around the subject when the image will become the first frame of a video.
